title: Winning in more than one place
question: Which businesses and organizations win in two or more different drawings, grant programs or pools, and which of them are also City payees, employers of campaign donors or lobbyists’ clients?
finding: 20 organizations and firms appear as a winner or member in two or more different places. 4 of the 8 entrants in the 2026 neighborhood liquor-licence drawing are also on the 2026 Storefront Opportunity Grant list (4 joined through the business registry, not by name alone), 2 of them ranked within the licences available; 3 firms hold places in three or more Public Works pools at once; 13 organizations won in more than one grant or credit program. 9 of them are profiled City payees and 7 have staff recorded as campaign donors.
how: A "place" is one program: the State liquor drawing, the Storefront Opportunity Grant, Community Challenge Grants, Arts Commission grants (the two files count as one program), State housing credits, or one Public Works pool. Names are matched by exact normalised name or shared owner-group. Liquor entrants and storefront recipients are joined through the City’s business registry: the grant’s business address must be a registered location of the entrant’s owner name, or the names must be the same. City payments, staff donations and lobbying come from this project’s profiles of City-funded organizations. 2 rows of the storefront table had a business name split by a number in it; the stray part was put back before matching.
limits: Unless a row says "Registry" or "Owner-group", it is a name match and two bodies can share a name. The liquor licences are limited to specified census tracts and all 4 matches are listed by the grant program under Bayview, so a new restaurant there could naturally seek both a grant and a licence; an arts organization that runs a neighborhood project fits two grant programs; and an engineering firm with several specialties can qualify for several pools. Donations by an organization’s staff are personal donations, matched by the employer the donor wrote down. The profiles cover City-funded nonprofits, so firms show no payment figure here even when the City pays them.
